description: JSON-RPC methods exposed by co.rsk.rpc.Web3RskImpl -- the class JsonRpcWeb3ServerHandler hands jsonrpc4j via service.getClass(), which is the dispatch surface and is three methods wider than the org.ethereum.rpc.Web3 interface -- that are deliberately absent from the published reference under doc/rpc/methods/. Every method must be either documented there or listed here with a reason and a basis; co.rsk.rpc.JsonRpcDocCoverageTest fails the build otherwise. The governing rule is that a method a default node does not serve does not appear in the published reference; those entries carry basis "configuration", and a configuration change is what could invalidate them. The remaining entries carry basis "editorial": they rest on judgement no configuration change can touch. The basis is a label. The guard checks that an entry is exposed, undocumented, justified and declares a recognised basis -- never that the reason written on it is still true, and never a "configuration" entry against the resolved node configuration. So if a namespace is enabled tomorrow, its entries keep passing while claiming the node does not serve it; the bases are what make that cheap to find by hand. This file sits at doc/rpc/ root and never inside methods/, which the generator loads wholesale.
